title: Unawareness during account registration
description: Homeowner registers account and enrolls cameras/sensors without full awareness of how personal data, device locations, and sensor details will be processed or shared by the Home Hub system.
assumptions: Homeowner is providing identifiable personal data and home layout info via the enrollment process.

title: Detectability of home surveillance setup
description: The registration and enrollment flow in transit reveals metadata about the homeowner setting up cameras/sensors, making the activity detectable and potentially linkable to a specific household.
assumptions: Flow occurs over a network where traffic analysis is possible.
uncertainty_note: Context does not explicitly cover network metadata threats for this flow.

title: Disclosure of personal and device enrollment data
description: Home Hub receives and stores account details plus camera/sensor enrollments, risking disclosure of sensitive home security information if access controls or storage are inadequate.
assumptions: Data includes identifiable info and potentially video feed metadata.

title: Detectability of guest access via code entry
description: Observing the communication flow of the temporary access code allows detection of the guest user's involvement and participation in unlocking the door, without needing access to the data content itself.
assumptions: The code entry communication or side-effects (e.g. door unlock event) can be observed by an adversary.
uncertainty_note: Grounded in retrieved context [5] on Detecting threats via observed communication or system responses.

title: Guest unawareness of logging implications
description: The guest user may be unaware that entering the temporary access code at the Home Hub results in processing or storage that links their action to identity or timing data.
assumptions: Guest assumes the temporary code is anonymous and non-tracked.

title: Non-repudiation of door access event
description: Processing the access code at the Home Hub creates irrefutable evidence of the guest's specific action, which the guest cannot later deny.
assumptions: The system logs successful code entries with timestamps or identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Context [3] confirms Nr applies to ExternalEntity->Process flows; specific tree node chosen by judgement.

title: Disclosure of sensor events in local log
description: The Local Event Log stores motion/door/sensor events which may disclose sensitive information about home occupancy, routines or specific activities if the datastore is accessed or compromised.
assumptions: Events contain timestamps and sensor IDs that can reveal personal patterns.

title: Linkability of events over time
description: Storing sequential sensor events in the log enables linking multiple events to the same household or individual, building behavioral profiles.
assumptions: No anonymization or aggregation applied to the log entries.

title: Unawareness of logging
description: Home Hub writes events without ensuring users are aware that their sensor data is being persistently logged locally.
assumptions: No user notification or consent mechanism for the logging action.
uncertainty_note: Context does not specify user interface details

title: Unprotected upload of sensitive video clips
description: Home Hub (P1) shares recorded camera clips containing personal data (e.g. faces, activities) to cloud storage without sufficient encryption or access controls at the point of sharing, leading to potential disclosure.

title: Linkability via upload metadata
description: The data flow DF4 carries metadata (timestamps, device IDs, IP addresses) that can link the Home Hub's video clips to a specific user or household identity during transit.

title: Detectability of video storage activity
description: Cloud Video Storage (DS2) receiving and storing clips makes the existence of surveillance activity detectable to cloud providers or attackers monitoring storage access patterns.

title: Motion alert data disclosure to backend
description: The Home Hub forwards real-time motion alerts (indicating home activity/presence) to the Mobile App Backend, transferring personal data across the system boundary to a service provider component. This may violate data minimality if the alert contains more detail than strictly necessary or if the backend's access is not sufficiently scoped.
assumptions: Motion alerts are considered personal data as they reveal user behavior and occupancy in a private home setting.
uncertainty_note: Context [4] and [5] directly support Dd for transfers of personal data; Dd.4 applies to exposure to involved parties like the backend.

title: Disclosure of motion events via push notification
description: The motion-detected notification pushed from the backend to the homeowner's phone may contain or imply sensitive details about home activity (e.g., presence/absence patterns). If the channel lacks strong encryption or uses an intermediary push service, this data could be disclosed to unintended parties in transit.
assumptions: Notification payload includes event details or metadata; standard mobile push mechanisms (APNS/FCM) are involved even if not explicitly modeled.

title: Detectability of home events from notification traffic
description: Observing the existence, timing, or frequency of push notifications on the flow can reveal that motion events are occurring at the property, enabling an observer to detect occupancy or activity patterns without accessing payload content.
assumptions: Traffic metadata (source/destination, volume, timing) is visible to network observers or the push provider.

title: Homeowner unawareness of notification data handling
description: The homeowner may be unaware of how the received notification data is stored, logged, or further processed on the phone or by the OS notification service, leading to unintended secondary use or retention of sensitive event information.
assumptions: Phone OS or app retains notification history; user has not reviewed privacy settings for notifications.

title: Users unaware of third-party analytics sharing
description: Mobile app backend shares device-usage analytics with external cloud vendor; end users may not be informed or may not understand the extent of this sharing.

title: Disclosure of usage patterns to analytics vendor
description: Even aggregated analytics can reveal sensitive usage behaviors when processed or stored by the external vendor, especially if re-identification becomes possible over time.

title: Linkability through flow metadata
description: The existence and timing of the analytics data flow between backend and vendor can be used to link app instances or user cohorts to specific external services.
uncertainty_note: Aggregation reduces but does not eliminate metadata-based linking risks; context does not explicitly cover flow metadata threats.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: The mobile app backend may store or cache the retrieved video clip longer than necessary for playback purposes.
assumptions: Backend could temporarily store videos for performance or logging reasons upon receipt.
uncertainty_note: Context provides this node for storage limitation; applying here upon data receipt/processing at P2 with moderate confidence as flow involves retrieval not primary storage.
